title: CalPro: Prior-Aware Evidential Conformal Prediction with Structure-Aware Sensitivity Bounds for Protein Structures
claim: Theoretical coverage-degradation bounds are conservative yet closely track the empirical decline as distribution shift grows, across real and synthetic shifts.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, left-to-right, dashed bound under solid empirical curve
description: Two side-by-side line plots share the same format. The left panel is titled 'Modality shift (X-ray → cryo-EM)' and uses blue lines. The right panel is titled 'Synthetic perturbations' and uses red lines. Both plot coverage (y-axis, about 0.875 to 0.900) against shift magnitude epsilon (x-axis, 0.0 to 0.3). Each panel has a dotted grey horizontal line at the nominal 0.900 coverage. A solid line shows empirical coverage, which falls roughly linearly from 0.900. A dashed line shows the theoretical bound. It starts at the same point, curves slightly below the empirical line, and ends just under it. A legend in the lower left lists Bound, Empirical and Nominal. Light grid lines run behind the curves. At the far left, a stray fragment of math text ('b(x) stal') is cropped in. The eye goes first to the diverging lines in each panel.
caption: Empirical coverage vs. PAC-Bayesian bound from Corollary 4.3 under increasing shift magnitude ϵ for modality shift (left) and synthetic perturbations (right). The curves show that the bound is conservative but tracks the empirical degradation closely.
abstract: Deep protein structure predictors such as AlphaFold provide confidence estimates (e.g., pLDDT) that are not calibrated and degrade under distribution shifts across experimental modalities, temporal changes, and disordered regions. We introduce \textbf{CalPro}, a prior-aware evidential conformal framework for shift-robust uncertainty quantification. CalPro combines three components: (i) a geometric evidential head outputting Normal Inverse Gamma distributions via graph neural networks; (ii) a differentiable calibration surrogate that shapes representations during training, followed by split-conformal calibration for finite-sample coverage; and (iii) domain priors (disorder, flexibility) encoded as soft constraints on predicted uncertainty. Theoretically, we derive structure-aware \emph{sensitivity bounds} for coverage degradation under distribution shift using PAC-Bayesian control over ambiguity sets, quantifying how miscoverage increases with model complexity and shift magnitude. Empirically, CalPro achieves at most 5 percentage points coverage degradation across modalities compared to 15 to 25 points for baselines, reduces calibration error by 30\% to 50\%, and improves downstream docking success from 52\% to 75\% when filtering by uncertainty. The framework extends beyond proteins to structured regression tasks where priors encode local reliability.
